_README: claude-jig settings. The hook entries below configure the four portable engines: guardrails.js (pre-write blocking/warning), post-edit-check.js (post-write typecheck/lint/build), session-start.js (read-only orientation — prints the pack status + recommended next step at session start so anyone knows what to do; fail-open, never blocks), and workflow-stop.js (a dormant, read-only Stop-event check — it can only ever ask Claude to finish one already-owed, already-authorized check obligation on a goal that explicitly registered for this; nothing in this release can turn it on — so it silently does nothing, by design; fail-open on every other input, exactly like the other three). The permission allow/deny lists are a conservative starting point — widen `allow` to match your toolchain (the bootstrap command will suggest entries from your repo). Two things to know before you widen it. First, an `allow` entry matches a command PREFIX, so it cannot exclude a destructive flag: `Bash(find:*)` would also permit `find -delete` and `find -exec <anything>`, and `Bash(git branch:*)` would permit `git branch -D`. That is why the shipped list stops at plain inspection commands and leaves anything with an obvious mutating mode to the prompt — treat an allow entry as convenience, never as a safety guarantee (`cat` can still write via a redirect, and `git diff`, `git log` and `git show` accept the diff option `--output=<file>`). Second, `deny` filters enumerated dangerous patterns and is NOT a contract gate: it cannot enforce a project rule like "only the fixed check command may run, no arbitrary shell" — a command that simply drops the matched token passes, and adding more deny patterns does not close that gap. The permission prompt you answer is the real boundary; a command `deny` did not block is not thereby sanctioned. NOTE: `permissions.defaultMode` is set to `plan` as the requested starting mode — remove that key if you don't want it. If this project already had a settings.json, the installer left it untouched and these settings landed as settings.pack.json: proposed configuration that can coexist with already configured hooks. Run /go or /bootstrap-claude-pack to compare live settings and propose only missing hook entries and permissions, preserving existing hooks and custom settings. If merging by hand, add missing entries only; do not replace the `hooks` block. The sidecar proves neither active nor dormant hooks. Configured wiring and direct engine probes do not establish host dispatch; runtime dispatch remains unknown without actual host evidence. Project-specific tuning lives in .claude/guardrails.rules.json and .claude/workspaces.json, not here.
